note:
Re-run of the 'What Slows Skin Repair?' diagram. Malcolm, 2026-08-25: the underside of the skin is not good enough, it looks like a half-empty area; consult professional diagrams to portray the right things; and use a reddish pink for the under-skin detail.

MY BRIEF ASKED FOR THE HOLE. The first version told every engine the deep zone should hold bundles that are 'thin, sparse and slack, drooping in loose unsupported curves WITH WIDE EMPTY GAPS BETWEEN THEM', because that was how I chose to signal loss of firmness. Each engine obliged and the result is an arch-shaped void under the skin. Exactly the same shape of error as the black band on the FAQ macro: a clause written to convey one idea produced a fault, and the engines were right both times.

WHAT THE RESEARCH SAYS, AND IT CONTRADICTS THE FIRST BRIEF. Ageing skin does not EMPTY. Sources below: the dermis stays full and what changes is that collagen becomes fragmented, thinned and disorganised, elastic fibres clump, fibroblasts fall in number and activity, and the dermal-epidermal junction FLATTENS. That last one is the single most characteristic change and the first brief did not have it at all. So the deficit now reads as degradation and disorder in a full dermis, never as a void.

  - Baumann 2007, J Pathol — aged skin shows epidermal and dermal atrophy, FLATTENING OF THE RETE RIDGES, and reduced numbers of fibroblasts and mast cells.
  - The Pathobiology of Skin Aging, Am J Pathol 2020 — rete pegs at the dermal-epidermal junction gradually flatten, contributing to wrinkle formation; photo-aged skin is characterised by ELASTOSIS, with fragmented and thickened elastic material.
  - StatPearls, Histology: Dermis — PAPILLARY dermis is loose areolar tissue carrying the CAPILLARY LOOPS that feed the epidermis and projecting as finger-like DERMAL PAPILLAE; RETICULAR dermis beneath is dense, thick type-I collagen bundles; the hypodermis below holds ADIPOSE LOBULES.
  - Lumen / Oregon State Anatomy — the papillary layer interlocks with the stratum basale as papillae and rete ridges; two vascular plexuses, one at the papillary-reticular boundary and one at the dermis-subcutis boundary.

FIVE STRUCTURES THE FIRST VERSION SIMPLY DID NOT HAVE, and between them they are what fills the space: the interlocking papillae-and-ridge junction, the capillary loops rising into each papilla, a papillary layer distinct from the reticular one, fine elastic fibres woven among the collagen, and fat lobules at the very bottom. The dermis is also given a stated share of the frame — the lower half of the block, at least twice the depth of everything above it — because 'an open deeper zone' let the engines make it a sliver.

REDDISH PINK IS ALSO THE ANATOMICALLY RIGHT ANSWER, not only Malcolm's preference. Dermis is eosinophilic — it is pink in every H&E section and in every professional cross-section — and it is densely vascular. The r3 note already established the principle: pink is anatomy, not a brand assignment. Blue and teal are now negated outright, since the dermis was blue in the first version and half the engines will default back to it.

CONSEQUENCE TO PUT IN FRONT OF MALCOLM, NOT TO DECIDE ALONE: the live 'Renewal Approach' image alongside this one has a CLINICAL BLUE fibre network. If this block goes reddish pink the pair no longer matches, and that block would need the same re-run. Flagged rather than actioned — it is his call which way the pair should go.

Still the DEFICIT STATE, so still no spheres, no shafts of light and no starburst glints anywhere: nothing is being applied. Square 2048x2048. CLASS B, no references, all six suppliers.

slots.title: causes r2 · a full, detailed, reddish-pink dermis that is degraded rather than empty
slots.prompt:
Soft three-dimensional medical explainer illustration in the style of premium skincare advertising and professional dermatology atlas plates: smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient background. Square format.

A block of skin is shown in cross-section, seen from a low three-quarter angle so both its top surface and its cut face are visible, filling most of the frame. The cut face is packed with structure from top to bottom and NO PART OF THE INTERIOR IS EMPTY.

FROM THE TOP DOWN. A thin outer layer of soft interlocking plates, pale peach-cream. Beneath it a few rows of flattened rounded translucent cells, the same pale peach-cream. THE WHOLE OF THE LOWER HALF OF THE BLOCK, at least twice the depth of everything above it, is dermis, and it is a warm reddish pink, colour hex D06A78, dense and glossy and completely filled.

THE DERMIS HAS TWO DISTINCT BANDS. The upper band is thin and finely textured, a loose fine mesh of slender pale pink threads, and rising into it from below are slender looped capillary vessels in a deeper red, colour hex A32B3C, each one a narrow hairpin loop reaching up toward the cells above. Below it the far thicker lower band is packed edge to edge with thick rope-like collagen bundles in deeper rose, colour hex B04A5C, crossing over and under one another in every direction, and woven through them are much finer wavy branching elastic threads in pale pink. Scattered among the bundles are small spindle-shaped cells with long tapering arms. Along the very bottom of the block sits a row of large rounded translucent fat lobules in pale buttermilk cream.

THE SKIN IS AGEING, AND THAT SHOWS AS DAMAGE AND DISORDER, NEVER AS EMPTINESS. The boundary between the pale cells above and the pink dermis below, which in young skin is a row of deep interlocking finger-like ridges, is here almost FLAT — only a few shallow worn-down bumps remain along it. The thick collagen bundles are frayed and broken into short ragged fragments that lie tangled and disorganised instead of running in ordered parallel waves, thinner than they should be but still filling every part of the space. The fine elastic threads are snarled into thickened clumps here and there. The spindle cells are few and small. The capillary loops are sparse and several are shortened stubs.

AND AT THE SURFACE. The outer plates are piled up in overlapping drifts several deep, edges lifting, dull and matte as though they have stayed far too long, and fine dark grey specks drift down out of the hazy air and settle across them and into the hollows between them. Where the junction beneath is flattest the top surface sinks into two or three broad soft-edged furrows.

Nothing is being applied to this block: the air above it holds only haze and the drifting specks, with no spheres, no beads, no beams of light and no bright glints anywhere. Flat even light, no hard shadow, shallow depth of field, the far edge dissolving into pale haze. Glossy and immaculate, but quiet and dull.
